feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iterations 0 to 5 gave the same outcome to within about 0.3 score points: max_error 0.060 to 0.061 m, one line-loss event per trial, no finishes. Spread (iteration 1), footprint (iteration 2), wheel track (iteration 3), wheel radius (iteration 4) and lead (iteration 5, which matched iteration 0 exactly) have not lifted the 0.06 m off-track floor. Iteration 6 (kp 3.0) was the only change that moved the score, and only on the slalom (14.39 to 45.18). So steering gain is the one controller lever that has shown an effect. The controller is held at iteration-6 values here, so this candidate tests mass alone, and no outcome is claimed for it. Next-race rules: (a) if line_loss_events fall below one and max_error drops below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, keep mass 0.5 kg and test kd (about 0.2) on the slalom to damp any oscillation; (b) if steering_oscillation rises sharply on the slalom while line loss is unchanged, the lower mass is over-steering, so add kd damping and do not change geometry again; (c) if the metrics match iteration 6 to four decimals, geometry is exhausted for this controller, and the pipeline should be checked as in iteration 4.
requested_changes: Keep mass at 0.5 kg with all other geometry from iteration 6 (sensors at y = 0.07 m, 16 mm footprints, +/-0.03 m spread, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m). Iteration 6 showed that the slalom responds to steering gain, and this race isolates how yaw inertia changes that response.

If mass 0.5 kg lowers max_error or line_loss_events on the oval and s-bend but raises slalom steering_oscillation, hold the geometry and add kd (0.05 to about 0.2) to damp the oscillation, as iteration 6 left kd untouched.

If mass 0.5 kg shows no change against iteration 6, test mass 0.4 kg (the contract minimum) as the last geometry lever, since iterations 0 to 5 show no other geometry change has moved the off-track floor.
